value.first: I'd start with the 3-Day Method: a three-day diaper-free reset at home. It works because diapers hide the feeling of being wet, so a ready child learns urge-to-action fast. Prep this week: pick 3 clear days at home, put a potty in the room you live in, stock salty snacks and drinks she loves, and brief every adult on the same words. Skip it if she's constipated or a big change is landing. If you can't clear three days, gradual child-led learning is the gentler route.
value.second: Day 1: say goodbye to diapers, bare from the waist down, and push fluids. The moment pee starts, carry her to the potty: "Pee goes in the potty." Say "Tell me when you need to go," not "Do you need to go?" Accident, every time: "You peed on the floor. Pee goes in the potty. Let's clean it up together." Never scold. Nap and night in a pull-up. Day 2: same, plus one 20-40 minute outing after a success, in loose pants with no underwear.
value.third: Day 3: repeat with a longer outing and prompt after waking, before leaving and before meals. Expect pees in the potty with prompting, not done: accidents go on for weeks, and poop usually lags. If nothing lands by day 3 or she panics, stop cheerfully and retry in 4-6 weeks. Call the doctor if she holds poop for 3+ days or poops are painful. Emma Hubbard, a paediatric OT, has a good walkthrough. I'll check in Thursday.
